output.brief: The departures are not about pay or market churn. Pay sits at the same level as the rest of the firm. The rival firm's premium is £3–5k, not £15k. Most leavers went to in-house roles or the regulator, and six of eight took equal or lower pay. The billable-target change applied everywhere, and other groups' attrition was steady. The problem is concentrated in Kestrel: 8 of its 11 associates resigned, against 1 of 13 other associates. Every Kestrel associate reports to Dorian Faulk, and he supervises no other matter. So the records can't separate heavy workload from his supervision style. Survey comments point to both: months of weekends, and late-night, publicly copied corrections. Kestrel places also went to the least-busy associates, which doesn't explain the exits. I'm confident about what to rule out and moderately confident the cause is inside Kestrel. I can't say which of the two factors dominates. Don't pay the retention bonus or close the review. Commission the confidential external interviews now (about £9k), structured to separate workload from supervision. Start tracking matter and supervising partner in attrition reporting. Decide on supervision changes or contract reviewers once the interviews are in. The review phase ends in December, so move quickly.
